ann_12.original: Black king two or more files right of the rook. 357 = 0.715 * max(0, (bk_file - wr_file) - 1) (exact to 0.0045 on all training rows; files a-h = 1-8). It is zero while the black king is on the rook's file or one file either side, then grows by 0.71 per file. Domain reading: a necessary condition for capture is |file difference| <= 1, and this unit flags one side of its violation. Evidence: zero on every draw; 0 of 8,743 positions with 357 > 0 are draws; largest restore gain of the leaves (linearised alone, AUC 0.997 -> 0.747). Feeds the output directly (-1.25), node 99 (+2.15, weight -2.69 at the output) and the rank hinge 2711 (+1.14). Self-assessment: meaningful.
ann_12.proposed: Switches on once the black king's file is more than about one file beyond the rook's file, and then pushes the predicted chance of a draw to almost nothing.

ann_13.original: Rook to the right of the black king (mirror of bk_right_of_rook), with a misplaced kink. 812 ~ 0.77 * max(0, (wr_file - bk_file) - 0.79) (r = 0.998), the constant -0.239 coming from dead_rank_unit via identity_812: 0 when the black king is on or right of the rook's file, 0.16 when the rook is one file right, 0.93 at two files, +0.77 per further file. 7455 = relu(0.234 - 1.17*812) is its soft complement (0.234 / 0.074 / 0), used only through the small 2804 term in far_from_rook. Domain reading holds for 'rook 2+ files right => no capture' (6 of 6,213 positions with 812 > 0.5 are draws), but the kink at 0.79 files also penalises the capture squares one file left of the rook (28% of draws get -0.31 logit), and the hinge is nearly redundant for ranking (linearised alone AUC 0.991, restore gain 0.02). Self-assessment: partial.
ann_13.proposed: Lowers the predicted chance of a draw a little when the rook stands on a file beyond the black king's file.

ann_14.original: Null (support-level, verified on the whole domain) plus a constant. 3965 = relu(-1.383*wr_rank_z - 2.375) has a negative pre-activation for every legal rook rank 1-8 (max -0.24 at rank 1), so it is never active (0 of 22,444 training rows) and zeroing it changes the output by exactly 0. 7180 = relu(3965 + 1.972) is therefore the constant 1.972; it only shifts biases (-0.239 into 812 via identity_812, +1.986 into 2804). No domain meaning: a bias carried by a dead unit. Self-assessment: closed-form-only (a verified Null).
ann_14.proposed: An inactive unit that changes no prediction.

ann_15.original: Rook two or more ranks above the black king. 2711 = relu(0.639*(wr_rank - bk_rank) - 0.65 + 1.136*357 + tiny file terms): within one file of the rook it is 0.639 * max(0, (wr_rank - bk_rank) - 1) (0 level or below, 0.01 at one rank above, 0.64 at two, +0.64 per further rank); the 357 input switches it on earlier when the black king is also 2+ files right of the rook. 3299, 5890, 8583 are always-on linear relays (total gain 3.29 into 99). Domain reading: |rank difference| <= 1 is needed for capture and this unit flags the 'rook too far above' side. Evidence: 99.96% of draws have 2711 < 0.2; 0 of 10,442 positions with 2711 > 0.5 are draws; linearised alone AUC 0.847 (restore gain 0.13). The opposite side (rook below the king) has no hinge anywhere in the network. Self-assessment: meaningful.
ann_15.proposed: Lowers the predicted chance of a draw when the rook stands above the black king.

ann_16.original: Additive 'too far from the rook' penalty. 99 = relu(2.15*357 + 3.29*2711(via 2711, 3299, 8583) + 0.154*2804 + c) with 2804 = 0.33 per black-king rank + 1.47*7455 + constant (always on, linear; r(2804, bk_rank) = 0.98). 99 is about 0.1 when the black king is next to the rook and 6.1 on average otherwise; it is active on 95% of rows and replacing its ReLU by the identity leaves AUC at 0.9970 (max output change 0.095), so the combination is effectively a weighted sum of the bk-right and rook-above hinges. Exits 99 plus 357 and 812, which also feed the output directly. Composition type: additive (sum before an almost always open ReLU).
ann_16.proposed: Lowers the predicted chance of a draw the further the black king is from the rook, combining checks on files and ranks.

ann_17.original: Root: a soft box around the rook, read as 'can the black king reach the rook?'. logit = 0.846 + 0.797*(wr_rank-4.52) - 0.620*(bk_rank-4.46) - 2.69*99 - 1.25*357 - 1.92*812. A five-term surrogate, logit = 0.49 + 0.72*(wr_rank - bk_rank) - 4.81*relu(bk_file - wr_file - 1) - 1.59*relu(wr_file - bk_file - 0.79) - 5.56*relu((wr_rank - bk_rank) - 1 + 1.27*relu(bk_file - wr_file - 1)), matches the logit with R^2 = 0.9996. Three sides of the box are hinges (black king 2+ files right of the rook, rook 1+ file right, rook 2+ ranks above); the fourth (rook below the king) is only the linear rank ramp, which also makes the predicted draw chance inside the box lopsided (0.70-0.78 rook one rank above, 0.39-0.44 one rank below, against a true draw rate of 0.9-0.98). Ground truth: draw = capture of an undefended rook or stalemate; the network's score ranks adjacency almost perfectly (AUC 0.99987), every predicted draw (p > 0.5) is an adjacent position, but only 62% of adjacent positions are predicted draws. The white king is not an input (wk_file, wk_rank unconnected: exact Null), so the defence of the rook (131 adjacent-but-defended positions, predicted 0.51) and stalemate (8, predicted 0.18) are invisible. Train AUC 0.9971, accuracy 0.960.
ann_17.proposed: The model gives a high predicted chance of a draw when the black king stands next to the rook; it adds the rook's and black king's ranks directly and ignores the white king.
